name: AI news / model releases / tech explainer
_channel: Live channel: 'AI Enthusiast' (@AIEnthusiast). Focus is in-depth, hands-on, benchmark-verified breakdowns of new AI model releases, tooling, architectures, and developer workflows.
audience: developers, AI practitioners, founders, tech enthusiasts 20-45, high intent, seeking verified evidence and deep technical breakdowns
_formats: THREE formats ship on this one channel. (1) single-story - the DEFAULT: one release, one delta, analyst voice. It IS the top-level title/script/pacing/images/sound/voice fields below (referenced, not duplicated, so the two can't drift). (2) compilation - formats.compilation: multi-story robotics/AI-hardware roundup, escalating register, merged in from the retired niches/robotics-news.json on 2026-08-01 (user's call: 'add it to ai news'). (3) explainer - formats.explainer: evergreen AI-education long-form (13-25 min, NOT tied to a dated release), added 2026-08-04 after reverse-engineering Sandeep Swadia's (@SandeepSwadia, 1.35M subs) title/thumbnail formula off multiple 500K-3.5M-view uploads - see formats.explainer._origin for the full pattern and what was and wasn't ported. Pick per video at intake: a model/tool release or one-story explainer on fresh news -> single-story; a dated multi-story roundup of the robotics/hardware moment -> compilation; a foundational AI concept/skill with no news hook, meant to stay relevant for months -> explainer. The channel's two promises and the mandatory close CTA apply to ALL THREE, but explainer's turnaround-speed promise is N/A (nothing to turn around on) - see formats.explainer.script._channel_promise_note. Tooling note: plan_runtime/plan_beats/video_spec/yt_research read the TOP-LEVEL fields (single-story) only - for compilation or explainer, use their override flags or work from that format's shares directly.

single-story._note: This format IS the top-level title/script/pacing/images/sound/voice of this file - referenced, not duplicated, so the two can't drift. The default format.

compilation.format_name: Robotics / AI hardware news compilation (multi-story, chronological)
compilation._origin: Merged from niches/robotics-news.json 2026-08-01 (user's call); that file is now a redirect stub. Its old _why_not_ai_news warning ('do not merge - different audience, different register') was resolved by keeping the two formats strictly separated INSIDE one file rather than blending them: single-story still bans caps-lock escalation and humanoid stock imagery; compilation still puts the escalation in the title/thumbnail (never the narration) for its own audience. First shipped compilation: videos/robotics-2026-updates-1 (2026-07-30, pre-merge).
compilation.audience: broad tech-curious 18-45, YouTube-native, came for spectacle and stays for specs; NOT the developer audience of the single-story format

rules: The escalation belongs in the TITLE and the THUMBNAIL. It does not belong in the narration - see honesty_guard.
Always carry the year. This genre is a dated snapshot and the year is the whole promise.
Always carry the series number (#1, #2). It sets up the next video and signals a running format.
Do not duplicate another channel's title string verbatim - same skeleton, own wording.

script._channel_promise_note: The channel's two promises apply to this format too: (1) the first ~170s must stand alone - cold-open-boom + story-1 together tell the viewer what happened and what it means (at an 18-min target their 0.05+0.10 shares land at ~162s - hold them tight; do not let the hook sprawl just because the video is long). (2) dark-side-close must carry the channel's mandatory CTA - subscribe (primary), like + comment (secondary) - written as one person talking, then the series tease. The turnaround angle is OPTIONAL here (compilations are dated snapshots, not breaking news) - if used, once, in the close.

structure.note: The year framed as a step-change, with the single hardest number available. Promise the list, then start it - no channel intro.
Open with the most concrete verified story. Per-segment shape: hook line -> what changed vs last year -> the specs/numbers -> what it means. Never open a segment on a target.
Same shape. Vary the opening line construction - eight identical segment openings is what makes a compilation feel like a content farm.
Same shape.
Same shape. Put a geography or category shift around here so the middle doesn't flatten.
Same shape. This is the retention trough - put the most viscerally relatable story here (the one that enters someone's house / body).
Same shape. Good slot for the software/brains story that explains why all the hardware suddenly works.
Same shape.
Same shape.
The step back. What all eight have in common. Earns the close - do not skip to the doom beat cold.

The counterweight: who loses, what is unresolved, who is objecting on the record. Then the channel CTA (subscribe primary, like + comment secondary - see _channel_promise_note), and the tease for the next number in the series.

voice_rules: Escalate with FACTS, not adjectives. 'One robot per hour, up from one per day' beats 'insanely fast'.
Every segment must contain at least one number and its source spoken aloud: 'per Figure's own production update', 'on the Q1 earnings call'.
Say the DATE on anything time-sensitive. This genre goes stale and dated claims are what keep it honest.
Verb discipline: SHIPPED / DEPLOYED / ANNOUNCED / TARGETS are four different words. Never let one stand in for another.
One honest limitation per segment, in the segment - not saved for the close. It is what separates this from a hype channel.
No 'and it only gets crazier from here' filler between segments. Hand off on a fact.
script.honesty_guard: This genre's failure mode is stating a TARGET as an ACHIEVEMENT - 'Tesla is making a million robots a year' when the filing says production starts slowly with an unpredictable rate. Every claim must be labelled: shipped / deployed / demoed / announced / projected. Company self-reported numbers must be attributed to the company out loud, not laundered into narrator fact. Prefer primary sources (company newsroom, SEC filings, conference programmes, named reporting) over SEO aggregator blogs; if a number only appears on aggregators, drop it. The title may escalate. The narration may not.
script._recency_note: A dated snapshot by design (the year is in the title), but the top-level recency_guard discipline still applies: research live at write time, re-verify every number that is more than ~48h old, state dates on time-sensitive claims.

images.style: industrial robotics, factory floor, robot arms, assembly line, lab, dark high-contrast tech palette with hard rim light
avoid: humanoid staring at camera in a field
images._facts_go_on_cards: Stock photos carry ATMOSPHERE only. Every number, spec, price and date belongs on a code-rendered spec/stat card, never spoken over an unrelated robot photo - that mismatch is the exact thing that makes a compilation look like a content farm. Real company footage, where the user supplies it, always beats both.

sound._bed_gain_note: MEASURED, not guessed. tech-pulse's own mean is -21.0 dB, so the old -15 put the bed at ~-36 dB and it lifted a speech gap by +0.4 dB (inaudible). -6 puts it ~6 dB under the voice in gaps, ~16 dB under while ducked. If you swap the bed clip, re-measure ITS mean and re-derive this number.
sound._note: Segment transitions want a real transition cue - this genre is 8 hard turns and the sound is what marks them. Measure every cue against the pre-SFX render; do not chase a quiet clip with gain.

voice.tone: energetic documentary narrator, escalating but never breathless
voice.tts_voice_hint: Channel default (Andrew per channel-persona.ai-news.json - the voice IS the channel identity) unless the user overrides per video. Pre-merge, robotics-2026-updates-1 shipped with en-US-GuyNeural at a slight rate lift; do not silently switch back to Guy without the user's call.

explainer.format_name: AI education explainer (evergreen, no news hook)
explainer._origin: Added 2026-08-04. Reverse-engineered from Sandeep Swadia's (@SandeepSwadia, 1.35M subs) catalog, all recent uploads 13-25 min and 480K-3.5M views: 'You're Not Behind (Yet): Learn AI Agents in 13 Minutes' (1.7M), 'You're Not Behind (Yet): How to Learn AI in 17 Minutes' (3.5M), 'How To Use Claude Better Than 99% Of People' (1.5M), 'Give Me 18 Minutes and I'll Make you Dangerously Smart (with AI)' (2.2M). Pattern extracted, not cloned - see honesty note below on what was deliberately NOT ported.
explainer._honesty_note: The source creator's thumbnails are built on a real, on-camera face (packaging checklist rule 11: ~89% of 2026 breakouts use a face or high contrast; his uses a face). This channel is faceless (no media/library/faces kit, confirmed openai-hf-hack precedent) - do NOT fake a host or imply one exists. Substitute: rules 2-4 of the packaging checklist (high contrast + thick-outline text + two-tone hook) are the load-bearing device instead, same as every other format on this channel. What WAS ported honestly: the title formula (concrete promise + explicit time-box, or percentile-superiority framing), the evergreen/no-news-hook positioning, and the content mechanism his comments credit (a plain-language contrast reframe - 'most people do X, the real shift is Y' - taught through one concrete analogy, not jargon).
explainer.audience: same base audience as the channel (developers, founders, tech-curious 20-45) but here they're not checking for breaking news - they want an actual skill/concept explained well enough to use it this week

title.formula: EITHER (a) [concrete promise] + explicit time-box: 'Learn/Understand [X] in [N] Minutes', OR (b) percentile-superiority: '[Skill] Better Than 99% Of People' / '[N] [Things] That Put You Ahead of 99%'
rules: The minute count in the title must roughly match the actual runtime (+/- ~2 min) - it's a keepable promise, not a round number picked for the title.
No 'SHOCKING' / 'INSANE' - same house rule as every other format on this channel, this audience reads it as a content farm.
Name a concrete, checkable skill or concept, never vague curiosity ('the AI trick nobody tells you' fails this; 'Learn AI Agents in 13 Minutes' passes).

script._channel_promise_note: The channel's SECOND promise (the 3-minute verdict mechanism) does not apply here - there is no release to deliver a verdict on. The FIRST promise (real, checkable, no overclaiming) still applies: don't claim a skill takes 'N minutes' if the video actually needs more runtime to teach it honestly. Still close with the mandatory CTA (subscribe primary, like+comment secondary) exactly like every other format.

structure.note: Name the common wrong mental model plainly, stated as a fact the viewer will recognize in themselves - not a tease. This IS the retention loop opener: name what the video will fix and be honest that it gets fixed by the end.

The 'most people do X, the real shift is Y' turn - one clean sentence, then ONE concrete analogy that carries the rest of the video (a driver vs a system that decides the next turn, etc). If you can't produce the analogy, the concept isn't understood well enough to teach yet - CLAUDE.md's own rule, applies doubly here since this whole format's job is teaching.

The actual how: break the skill/concept into 3-5 concrete, memorable steps or components. Each one gets a plain-language name and a one-line gloss, never left as jargon. This is the load-bearing teaching beat - most of the runtime lives here.

A real, concrete walkthrough applying the framework to one specific case (a real prompt, a real workflow) - not an abstract restatement. Evidence-first: if the example involves a real tool's UI, use a real screenshot/screencast, not an invented mockup.

Where this breaks, what it doesn't solve, what still requires real skill/effort underneath the AI. Mandatory - this is the trust beat and the same honesty_guard as every other format on this channel applies. (Source-pattern comments specifically flagged when a video oversold ease of implementation - don't repeat that miss.)

MANDATORY every video: (1) one line on why this channel teaches this (evidence-first, no hype - the same real differentiator as the news formats, reworded for a teaching context), (2) subscribe as the primary ask, (3) like + comment their take as secondary asks. One person talking, not a checklist.

voice_rules: Teach a tired 12-year-old (CLAUDE.md GROWTH RULE 6 applies at full strength here - this format's entire job is comprehension, more than any other format on this channel).
One idea per sentence, jargon glossed in the same breath, an analogy for every mechanism.
Never explain what a well-known tool/model IS if the audience already knows it - go straight into the concept being taught.
script.honesty_guard: Same as the rest of this niche: every concrete claim about what a tool/workflow can do needs to be something actually demonstrated on screen, not asserted. Do not understate the real engineering/setup effort behind an AI workflow to make it sound like 'type a prompt and it's done' - the source pattern's own top comment called this out as the weak point to avoid repeating.
script._recency_note: This format is deliberately evergreen - it should NOT reference a specific dated release as its hook. If a concept example needs a live tool, note the tool version once and keep the teaching point tool-agnostic where possible so the video doesn't go stale in weeks like the other two formats do.

images.style: same clean product/UI screenshots and dark technical palette as single-story - this format still needs real tool screenshots for the worked-example beat, not stock photos of people at laptops

sound._note: Lower density than the news formats (low, not medium) - this is a sustained teaching format and constant SFX competes with comprehension. Reserve SFX for framework-step reveals and the worked-example beat, not every sentence.

voice.tts_voice_hint: Consider calm-explainer delivery mode (not breaking-news) even on the channel-default voice, since this format is not news - confirm with the user before locking a second delivery mode for one channel.

Raw data: docs/research/ai-news.json / .txt. Strongly CONFIRMS the 'point of view beats a summary' finding already in docs/IMPROVEMENT-QUEUE.md's 'What is actually working on AI channels' section - every real top-vpd title above is a blunt opinion ('is a freak', 'About To Pop The AI Bubble', 'Forget NVIDIA'), not a neutral description. Lean harder into the verdict beat's opinionated framing. RUNTIME TENSION worth flagging: the 30d window's actual top-vpd AI content ran 8-32 min (median 15 min across all AI content, not just this channel's exact lane) - noticeably longer than this channel's [3,10] min / hard_max 12 positioning. The under-3-min VERDICT mechanism (script.brand_promise) is still sound regardless of total runtime, but this is a data point for whether the evidence section should be allowed to run longer on major releases, not something changed here unilaterally.

delta: beats its own flagship at half the price

rules: Name the model/company in the title - this audience searches by name.
Numbers must be real and sourced. This audience checks, and being wrong once costs the channel.
No 'SHOCKING' / 'INSANE'. It reads as a content farm to this audience specifically.

script._target_minutes_note: RE-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: length now scales with how much the release actually warrants, not a fixed cap. A minor point-update might still land near 3-4 min; a major flagship release with real benchmarks/pricing/ecosystem impact can run 8-10. Propose the specific number for that video based on story depth, per make-video/SKILL.md's 'always propose a length for approval' rule - don't default to the top or bottom of the range without a reason tied to that release's actual substance.
script.brand_promise: Two promises, both real and checkable: (1) DEPTH & EVIDENCE - every model/feature breakdown includes real benchmarks, screen recordings, code executions, and honest architectural trade-offs; (2) TURNAROUND - covering new breakthroughs fast without sacrificing technical accuracy. Be honest about what's actually achievable. Never phrase promises as an announcer slogan; say it conversationally.
script._structure_phase_note: Natural narrative flow: Hook -> Context -> Deep Architecture & Benchmarks -> Live Code & Agent Evaluation -> Honest Limitations & Trade-offs -> Actionable Conclusion & CTA.

structure.note: The single most surprising true fact, stated flatly with its key metric. Also opens the retention curiosity loop.
What existed before, explaining why the breakthrough or release matters.
What changed and what it means for developers, builders, and AI enthusiasts, backed by headline benchmarks.
The deep dive: hands-on tests, terminal code runs, benchmark tables, pricing details, and screen recordings.
Where it falls short, limitations, trade-offs, and fine print. Non-negotiable for building genuine trust.
Mandatory closing: summarize the takeaway, ask for subscribe/comments on the findings, and tease what is next.

voice_rules: Precise, fast, no filler. This audience punishes padding with the back button.
Cite as you speak: 'on Artificial Analysis', 'per their own model card'.
Never state a benchmark from memory - it must come from a captured source.
This audience is not naive - they already follow this space. Never explain what a well-known model/company is; go straight to what's new.
script.honesty_guard: Every number needs a real captured source (screenshot or page). If a source cannot be captured, drop the claim and say so on screen - see EVOLUTION 'Some official sources are unusable'.
script.recency_guard: This niche can go stale in HOURS, not months - unlike a genre where a year-old fact still holds, a claim here can be wrong by the time of upload even if it was right when researched. Rules: (1) never write from memorized/cutoff knowledge - always research live at write time per CLAUDE.md's AssemblyAI-style 'fetch live docs' discipline, applied to the news itself; (2) if research for this video is more than ~48h old, re-verify every number against the primary source before scripting, don't assume it still holds; (3) state the info's own timestamp on screen where it matters ('as of the announcement post', 'as of July 30') so the viewer can judge freshness themselves; (4) if a detail is still shifting (rollout %, pricing not final, benchmark contested), say so explicitly rather than presenting it as settled.

images.style: clean product/UI screenshots, benchmark charts, dark technical palette

sound._bed_gain_note: Corrected 2026-07-30 (was -14, never measured). tech-pulse's own mean is -21.0dB; -14 put the effective bed near -35dB, inaudible against a ~-25dB speech-gap floor. -6 lands it at the validated -27dB target. Re-derive if the bed clip changes: bed_gain_db = -27 - <clip's measured mean dB>.
